Sweep alignment is a standard procedure when aligning wideband amplifiers, and is always required when aligning television tuners. The IF section of an FM broadcast receiver, however, has a narrower bandwidth than a television tuner, and alignment can be accomplished with a standard signal generator if it is done carefully.

The output of the mixer is at pins 4 and 5. T1 and C4 make up a balanced output tuned circuit which accepts the IF frequency of 10.7 MHz, the mixer difference output, and rejects the three higher output frequencies.

The local oscillator frequency is always 10.7 MHz below the desired tuned frequency. The output of the mixer will be the tuned frequency, the local oscillator frequency, the two frequencies added together, and the difference between the two frequencies, 10.7 MHz, which is the IF frequency.
